action_items: Low priority: refresh IL/USA branch admin seed users (ofir1@bashds.com, ofir2@bashds.com) or update /app/memory/test_credentials.md so branch_admin-scoped tests can run (currently skipped, not a product bug).
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/routes/jobs.py list_jobs expected branch: when `use_expected` is true the code loads ALL candidates matching the scope/search/status into memory to compute expected dates, then paginates. For small datasets (<10k) this is fine, but at larger scale this becomes O(N) per request and defeats paging. Consider caching expected_for_jobs results or a scheduled denormalization into a jobs.expected_verbal_date field. Non-blocking at current volume (~124 jobs).

/app/backend/routes/shipments.py list_shipments: `base['job_ids'] = {'$elemMatch': {'$in': ids}}` is a correct branch filter, but when a branch has thousands of jobs the `ids` array embedded in the query can exceed MongoDB document limits. Non-blocking at current scale.

/app/backend/routes/shipments.py list_shipments.completed_count: computed BEFORE the status clause is added to `base`, which is correct per spec ('completed_count counts only completed'). The variable name is clear but a comment would help future readers.
/app/backend/routes/stones.py list_stones still calls get_all_stones (full in-memory pass) and then paginates — same scalability caveat as jobs/list expected branch. Fine at current volumes.

Minor: /api/jobs/list `page_size` is capped at 200 — good; but if a UI ever requests >200 the server silently clamps. Consider returning the effective page_size in the response (already done) and documenting the cap in OpenAPI.
